analysis:
This batch contains only test code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot. AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift adds two @testable setters at head lines 120-126: setAutopilotResidentSinceForTesting and setAutopilotLeaseForTesting. The other units are new test suites: SelectedModelPlacementPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryFixture, SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryTests and SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests. None of these files ship in the provider binary, so they add no runtime attack surface.

The tests describe new production behavior whose source is not in this batch. A SelectedModelRecovery queue retries selected models that a skipped startup preload or an Autopilot operation displaced. Checks back off from 30s to 600s. Recovery may evict an adopted model outside the selection only after its hold, its minimum dwell, its minimum idle time and any per-model lease have passed, and never a pinned or running-selection model. An expired-hold busy adoption is first released (no longer advertised), then evicted after its requests drain. Recovery pauses during drain, autopilot operations, model switches, startup preload, other loads and a live lease. An attempt in progress reports busy as preload.

The security-relevant contract is the add-on hold interaction (TB-012, T-059, A-018). Per SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests.swift head lines 202-231, an add-on hold must cancel an in-flight recovery load, and later checks must pause as draining, so models do not load beside VMs. Integration should verify in production source that the recovery attempt honors the model-load fence (T-059) and the hold's drain/cancellation. It should also confirm that recovery cannot bypass the existing load gates, including weight-hash and pinned-checkpoint checks (T-012/T-027). The test at SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests.swift lines 199-238 suggests the real Nemotron Super gate still runs.

Release and eviction change routing availability (A-018); in-flight requests are allowed to finish before shutdown. No crypto, attestation, authorization or prefix-cache (T-041) changes are visible. Missing production source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
